description: Explainable AI (XAI) engines make machine decisions transparent: instead of a bare prediction, they produce the reasons — which inputs mattered, which rules fired, what would change the outcome, and how confident the system is. t: Current Research State of Explainable AI (XAI) Engine
title: Current Research State of Explainable AI (XAI) Engine
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: SHAP, LIME, integrated gradients, and counterfactual methods became standard tooling; regulators (EU AI Act) began requiring explanations for high-risk systems. Research focuses on faithful explanations (not plausible-sounding rationalizations), explanations for large language models, and causal methods. The gap: explanations can mislead as easily as they inform. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Explainable AI (XAI) Engine currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
